SOCIAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which school transport is safe? (1 mark)
   A. A vehicle with no seats
   B. A vehicle approved by school and parents
   C. A stranger's car
   D. An overloaded vehicle

2. Which item usually comes first on an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. Suggestions
   B. Opening prayer or song
   C. Reports
   D. Closing remarks

3. Which is a good school rule? (1 mark)
   A. Write on walls
   B. Break desks
   C. Fight in class
   D. Come to school on time

4. Who elects the governor? (1 mark)
   A. The president alone
   B. Registered voters in the county
   C. The chief
   D. The teachers

5. What is a timeline? (1 mark)
   A. A picture of a school
   B. A weather chart
   C. A line showing events in the order they happened
   D. A kind of ruler

6. Which area is most likely to be sparsely populated? (1 mark)
   A. A fertile highland
   B. A busy town
   C. A lakeshore with fish
   D. A very dry area with little rain

7. What is a product? (1 mark)
   A. A worker
   B. A raw material
   C. A tool
   D. A finished good that is made

8. Which is the correct way to write the in-between point that is between south and west? (1 mark)
   A. West-south
   B. West-south-west
   C. Sowest
   D. South-west

9. Which is a responsibility of a child? (1 mark)
   A. Bully others
   B. Respect others and study hard
   C. Skip school
   D. Steal

10. Why do many people live near rivers and lakes? (1 mark)
   A. Rivers are dangerous
   B. Lakes have no fish
   C. Rivers are always dry
   D. Water is available for drinking and farming

11. What is a plain? (1 mark)
   A. A lake with salt water
   B. Wide flat land
   C. A waterfall
   D. A steep mountain

12. Which country lies to the west of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Ethiopia
   B. Somalia
   C. Uganda
   D. Tanzania

13. What is public participation? (1 mark)
   A. Citizens leaving
   B. Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget
   C. Citizens hiding
   D. Citizens breaking laws

14. What is the best way to compare the sizes of two counties on maps? (1 mark)
   A. Compare the length of the names
   B. Use the same scale and compare the areas
   C. Count the number of towns only
   D. Guess without a map

15. Who leads a clan? (1 mark)
   A. Clan elders
   B. A cook
   C. A footballer
   D. A bus driver

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Give five people who serve your community and say how each helps. (5 marks)

17. Write a short motto for a school and say what it means. (3 marks)

18. List the steps for solving a conflict peacefully. (4 marks)

19. Name three child rights. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — A vehicle approved by school and parents
   Approved vehicles are safer.

2. B — Opening prayer or song
   Meetings begin with an opening.

3. D — Come to school on time
   Being punctual is a good habit.

4. B — Registered voters in the county
   Voters in the county elect the governor.

5. C — A line showing events in the order they happened
   A timeline shows events in order.

6. D — A very dry area with little rain
   Dry areas make farming and water supply hard.

7. D — A finished good that is made
   Products are the goods that come out of a factory.

8. D — South-west
   We say the north or south word first, so it is south-west.

9. B — Respect others and study hard
   Rights come with responsibilities.

10. D — Water is available for drinking and farming
   Water is a basic need.

11. B — Wide flat land
   A plain is a wide, flat area.

12. C — Uganda
   Uganda is Kenya's western neighbour.

13. B — Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget
   People take part in decisions.

14. B — Use the same scale and compare the areas
   To compare fairly we use maps drawn to the same scale.

15. A — Clan elders
   Clan elders lead the clan.

SECTION B
----
16. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example: farmer grows food, teacher teaches, nurse treats the sick, driver carries people and goods, trader sells goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each person with a correct service.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It means pupils should study well and be kind to others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for its meaning, 1 mark for showing action.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stop, calm down, talk and listen, find a solution together, and say sorry and forgive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step, up to 4.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: The right to education, to health care and to protection. Accept food, a name or play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each right.
